visible_text: In triangle PQR, points A and B lie on side PQ, points C and D lie on side QR, and points E and F lie on side RP. AB, CD and EF are chords of a circle with centre O such that AB = CD = EF. If ∠QPR = 38°, find the measure of ∠QOR.
reasoning: Equal chords of a circle are equidistant from the centre, so O is equidistant from all three sides of ΔPQR. Hence O is the incenter of ΔPQR, making QO and RO the internal angle bisectors of ∠PQR and ∠PRQ respectively. In ΔQOR, ∠QOR + ∠OQR + ∠ORQ = 180°. Since ∠OQR = ½∠PQR and ∠ORQ = ½∠PRQ, we have ∠QOR = 180° – ½(∠PQR + ∠PRQ). Using ∠PQR + ∠PRQ = 180° – ∠QPR gives ∠QOR = 180° – ½(180° – ∠QPR) = 90° + ½∠QPR. Substituting ∠QPR = 38°, ∠QOR = 90° + 19° = 109°. This corresponds to option A.
